title: Rough sleepers, shelter take-up and how MSF designs shelter spaces
asked: Mr Gabriel Lam asked whether MSF is concerned that 75% of surveyed rough sleepers were unreceptive to shelters and how shelter models are being redesigned, and how MSF interprets the finding that 95% sleep rough in the same location and whether that shapes outreach.
response: Mr Eric Chua said the 2025 Street Count found most rough sleepers pick sheltered, well-lit spots they know, near friends, family or work, and that many have homes but sleep rough after disagreements with family, friends or co-tenants. He said MSF and PEERS Network volunteers build trust before support is offered, and that shelters have been redesigned with partitioned bed spaces, shelves and wardrobes because privacy and personal space were key barriers. MSF has announced a $450,000 Partnership to Tackle Homelessness (PATH) fund for organisations trialling solutions. On the supplementary questions, he put the prevalence rate at about 75% and said the Street Count Report lists 730 transitional shelter bed spaces, with utilisation at about 66% as of September last year.

key_points.point: Most rough sleepers choose sheltered, well-lit locations they are familiar with, near friends and family, and some near their workplace.
key_points.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
key_points.quote: most rough sleepers choose to sleep in locations that are sheltered from the elements and are generally well-lit

key_points.point: Many rough sleepers have homes but sleep rough because of disagreements with family, friends or co-tenants.
key_points.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
key_points.quote: Many rough sleepers have homes to return to but rough sleep due to disagreements with family, friends or co-tenants.

key_points.point: Shelter units were redesigned with partitioned bed spaces, shelves and wardrobes after lack of privacy and personal space were identified as key barriers.
key_points.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
key_points.quote: MSF has partnered our shelter operators and re-designed the units with partitioned bed spaces, shelves and wardrobes

key_points.point: MSF announced a $450,000 Partnership to Tackle Homelessness (PATH) fund inviting organisations to trial solutions.
key_points.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
key_points.quote: MSF has also recently announced a $450,000 Partnership to Tackle Homelessness (PATH) fund

key_points.point: About 75% of rough sleepers on the streets do not wish to check into a shelter, with privacy and personal space the primary reason.
key_points.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
key_points.quote: The prevalence rate is about 75% based on the last street count.

key_points.point: The Street Count Report lists 730 transitional shelter bed spaces, with utilisation at about 66% as of September last year.
key_points.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
key_points.quote: we mentioned 730 transitional shelter bed spaces

left_open: A breakdown of rough sleepers who decline shelters specifically because of safety concerns or loss of autonomy, as distinct from rules and privacy.
How outreach strategies are tailored for rough sleepers who are reluctant to relocate to shelters.
